Wide_Rebalance_2pct.definition: wide 30%, enter on OPEN/EXTENDED, rebalance at 2%, hold through freezes

Narrow_Rebalance_1pct.definition: narrow 5%, enter on OPEN/EXTENDED, rebalance at 1%, hold through freezes

limits: True S is used for scoring only and never enters a feature or policy.
kappa/mu/jump are the G0 step-2 estimates; the block study varies only sigma estimation.
The observation-mapping parameters are estimated with true S as a diagnostic, not from P alone.
The estimated model resamples the 128 per-path sigma estimates; measurement noise in sigma is not deconvolved.
The block study uses new simulator paths to estimate sigma/kappa_P; it is a simulation study, not the frozen dataset.
D2' diagnostics are along-observed-history sensitivities, not a uniform sup over beliefs.

D2' W1 compares the identified posterior over log S_t with the naive point belief delta_{log P_t} (naive treats P as S); it is a one-dimensional log-S marginal, not the joint law over (S, eta, anchor).
D2' W1/TV/flip are plug-in estimates with kappa/mu/h/sigma treated as fixed; no confidence intervals are attached to the three terms (128 paths).

D2' naive AR(1) parameters (kappa_P, mu_P, sigma_all) are fitted per path (336 observations), so per-path kappa_P is noisy (e.g. 0.015 vs pooled 0.0028); this matches the step-5/6 per-path naive model, not step 5's pooled naive check.
D2' post-anchor W1 is checked against an oracle |log S_true - log P|; the pre-anchor filter cross-check covers only the R=0 segment, while post_update_check covers the OPEN R>0 update analytically.

D2' L_T=1 is stated in a metric that counts log S once; the literal Euclidean operator norm of the OPEN transition (which duplicates log S into the anchor coordinate) is sqrt(2)(1-kappa), a coordinate-duplication artifact.
D2' predictive TV is numerical integration of Gaussian one-step predictives; HALT gives TV=1 because the identified model knows P is frozen and the naive model does not.
Jumps (prob 0.003) are omitted in the D2' filter and predictive; both sides omit them.
D2' action-flip probability is first-order: positions come from the observed trajectory and the flip probability is the minimal-coupling Bernoulli disagreement |p_id-p_naive|.
Le Cam deficiency is not estimated in D2'; the predictive TV is the information-term estimate, and Le Cam only controls Bayes-optimal values.
Event-level conditional coverage uses observable pre-decision groups (onset action/distance/side); in_position is degenerate for both target policies (always in position), so the flat group is empty.
post_rebalance is a post-hoc boundary diagnostic, not a prediction-time condition; it is not a deployable conditional guarantee and cannot be fixed by pre-decision Mondrian calibration.

Conditional group coverage is descriptive: small groups are shown with binomial SE, worst_gap_n20 excludes groups with n<20, group kappa_conf is a plug-in KS distance without a bootstrap CI, and Prop 7 remains a marginal (not conditional) guarantee.

branch_union uses post_rebalance labels in calibration only; it is the minimal branch-aware fix that shows the width cost of branch-conditional coverage. It is not a test-time conditional method, and its branch labels are post-decision outcomes.

branch_kappa is a plug-in KS distance on branch sizes 16-112. The KS sampling floor under equal distributions is large (asymptotic iid mean 0.13-0.24 and 95% quantile 0.21-0.38 over these branch sizes), so raw kappa_conf is not evidence of shift without the null reference; kappa_excess is descriptive. The KS bound and the empirical trivial decomposition are both plug-in, not finite-sample guarantees; the trivial decomposition uses the evaluated method's observed overall coverage (marginal over branches) and is exact only when all non-coverage sits in that branch. The paired path bootstrap captures cross-tau dependence but treats branch labels as resampled outcomes. The iid KS null ignores the cross-tau path pairing; positive dependence typically narrows its dispersion, so the reference is conservative.

branch_union_joint compares the branch-union and the unmodified marginal pipeline on the same test events and folds. Coverage dominance (union coverage >= marginal coverage) is structural, because max(q_hold,q_rebalance) >= q_pooled per fold; the reported gain is one-sided and its SE is the binomial SE of the gain. The five-way taxonomy uses normal-approximation 95% intervals on branch sizes 16-112, is descriptive rather than simultaneous, and labels most small gains ambiguous. The width ratio is a calibration-side quantity for scale-family scores but includes the target base width for CQR. Cross-regime residual_gap/kappa is zero when the union covers and is not a calibrated error rate; the kappa bound is descriptive, not a prospective certificate.

Pre-decision Mondrian uses only onset_action/onset_distance/onset_side labels in interval construction; onset_action=rebalance has n=8 at tau=2, so most folds have no finite group quantile and fall back to the marginal quantile. The pre-group fix is therefore partial and fallback counts are reported.

Mondrian post_rebalance coverage is an evaluation diagnostic only; conditioning on that post-decision branch is impossible at prediction time, so pre-decision Mondrian is expected to leave the post-branch gap near its trivial bound.

config.episode_definition: pre-anchor to post-anchor; target policy starts from the observable position inherited from the path before the episode

state_groups.in_position: observable position before the pre-anchor action; degenerate for both target policies (always in position), so the flat group is empty
state_groups.onset_action: policy action at the pre-anchor decision: open (flat), rebalance (in position and |P_pre/anchor-1|>theta), or hold; computed from observed P and the inherited anchor
state_groups.onset_distance: near if |P_pre/anchor-1|/theta>0.5, else far; flat events (not in position) are far by construction (currently none)
state_groups.onset_side: P_pre above vs below the inherited anchor
state_groups.post_rebalance: observed policy action at the post-anchor decision (rebalance vs hold); a post-hoc outcome, not available at prediction time, reported only as a boundary diagnostic

conditional_metrics.worst_gap_n20: max(0, (1-alpha) - min group coverage) over groups with n>=cond_min_n; a shortfall from nominal, not a between-group range
conditional_metrics.group_kappa_conf: per-group KS distance between calibration and test scores; descriptive plug-in, no bootstrap CI

config.branch_union: branch-wise conformal on post_rebalance labels: per fold, compute separate conformal quantiles on hold and rebalance calibration events and issue the union/hull interval with the larger quantile; uses the post-decision branch label in calibration only, and is reported as the minimal width cost of branch-conditional coverage (not a test-time conditional method)
config.branch_kappa: per-branch KS distance between calibration and test score distributions, pooled within each post_rebalance branch (cross-tau directions only); kappa_excess subtracts the asymptotic iid KS mean sqrt(pi/2)ln2*sqrt((n_cal+n_test)/(n_cal*n_test)), and the paired path bootstrap resamples both the scores and the branch labels. Per branch it reports the KS bound 1-alpha-kappa_b and the empirical trivial decomposition 1-(1-c)/q_b from the evaluated method's observed overall coverage c (marginal over branches; for the branch-union output this is its branch_union.coverage, not the unmodified marginal pipeline; equal to the Prop-8 bound when c=1-alpha). Branch labels are deterministic given the frozen paths, so branch counts and null references are seed-invariant; the three-seed summary stores kappa_conf, SE, bound and trivial decomposition only.
config.branch_union_joint: joint coverage/width summary of the branch-union against the unmodified marginal pipeline on the same test events: per post_rebalance branch, marginal and union coverage with binomial SE, the paired coverage gain (union minus marginal; union coverage is a superset because max(q_hold,q_rebalance) >= q_pooled), the branch width ratio, and a five-way taxonomy (cost_only: marginal lower 95% CI >= 1-alpha; clear_gain: gain lower 95% CI > 0 and union not clearly below nominal; gain_but_fails: gain clear but union upper 95% CI < 1-alpha; fails_no_clear_gain: union clearly below nominal but gain not clear; ambiguous: neither). Cross-regime rows also carry the branch kappa, its 1-alpha-kappa bound, the bound slack and residual-gap/kappa ratio. Intervals are normal-approximation, descriptive and not simultaneous. The kappa_bound_1malpha stored here is unclipped, so it can be negative when kappa_b > 1-alpha (4 cross-regime branch cells). worst_gap_before/after use all branches and do not apply the n>=20 threshold of conditional.worst_gap_n20. The three-seed summary omits cal_n/cal_fraction because branch labels are deterministic given the frozen paths and seed-invariant.
config.pre_decision_mondrian: Mondrian conformal on pre-decision labels (onset_action / onset_distance / onset_side): per fold, a separate conformal quantile per calibration group, using the test point's group quantile. A group with no finite calibration quantile (n_cal < ceil((n_cal+1)(1-alpha))) falls back to that fold's marginal quantile; fallback counts are reported. post_rebalance labels are used only in the summary evaluation, never in interval construction.

phases.anchor: t = pre-anchor (last informative step before the freeze)
phases.post: t = post-anchor (first OPEN after the freeze)

config.w1: E|log S_t - log P_t| under the identified posterior; equals W1(posterior, delta_{log P_t}) (naive treats P as S)
config.tv: TV between identified and naive one-step predictives of log P_{t+1}, evaluated at the observed history
config.oracle_w1: mean |log S_true_t - log P_t| along the same histories, using the simulator's latent price for validation only

filter_consistency.note: filter_episode posterior at pre-anchor vs kalman_pre_belief (same Kalman equations; should be near machine precision). This covers only the noiseless EXTENDED segment (R=0); the OPEN update with R>0 is covered by post_update_check.

post_update_check.note: post-anchor OPEN update vs the analytic scalar Kalman identity var = P R/(P+R), mean = prior + P/(P+R)(y-prior), with P the filter's prior variance at post. Independent of _update_state; exercises the R>0 path that the pre-anchor cross-check misses.

contraction_check.note: I-KH spectral norm is a Euclidean proxy for the filter's mean-map Lipschitz constant, not the W1 constant; it is non-normal and can exceed 1, so a value >1 is NOT a violation of the W1 contraction. L_T=1 because additive transition noise can be coupled; this counts log S once, whereas the literal Euclidean norm of the OPEN transition (log S duplicated into the anchor coordinate) is sqrt(2)(1-kappa), a coordinate-duplication artifact. The finite-horizon episodes (H<=83) give a finite composition regardless; gamma L_Phi L_T < 1 is only needed for the infinite-horizon corollary. The per-step diagnostics below do not rely on it.

config.margin: |P_t/anchor-1| - theta at decision steps (in position, OPEN/EXTENDED); m>0 means the observed path rebalances
config.flip: |p_id - p_naive| = minimal-coupling probability that the rebalance decision at t+1 differs, where p_model = P(|P_{t+1}/anchor-1| > theta) under that model's predictive; positions are taken from the observed trajectory (first-order)

d2prime.note: D2' decomposition diagnostics: W1 estimation term, predictive-TV information term, and boundary/action-flip frequency. These are along-observed-history sensitivities, not a uniform sup over beliefs; the third block is a diagnostic refinement for observation-type policies, not an independent bound term.
